recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Future changes to access-denied response handling should be made in the consolidated source/security.html#AccessDenied section through a new Security work group decision, not by re-adding the old duplicated paragraph to http.html.
issue_request: FHIR-7921 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification security issue for FHIR-core-http. It proposed requiring 403 responses when clients are unauthorized, but the accepted motion was to add guidance that 404 should normally be the default unless there is a specific reason to return 403.
initial_application: Related FHIR-3310 first introduced 403/404 policy text to the RESTful API and Security pages in commit e99a4d5856. FHIR-7921 was explicitly applied in commit 6f4cc33a42 / SVN revision 6467, adding that 404 does not leak information and should be the default unless there is a specific reason to return 403.
additional_context: FHIR-9593 later concluded that the simple 403/404 advice duplicated on http.html and security.html was incomplete. Commit 268bdbbf8b implemented that later Published/Persuasive with Modification decision by replacing the duplicate REST-page paragraph with a pointer to Security and adding a fuller Access Denied Response Handling section covering empty search Bundles, 404, 403, and 401. Current source/security.html retains that section and current source/http.html links to it from security-sensitive interaction text.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Restoring the older FHIR-7921 paragraph would duplicate and partially roll back the later FHIR-9593 consolidation. The current source already tells implementers that response choice is policy/context dependent, that 404 protects against leakage, and that 403 should be used only when the client or user is well enough known to receive that information.
